hens_rule_text: up to 8 chickens allowed as an accessory use on lots with up to 4 dwelling units; no roosters
permit_notes: A Chicken Owner Registration/License ($10 fee) is required through the city's Building Inspection Division; applicants must first complete the free Wisconsin DATCP Livestock Premises Registration and provide that registration number. The Zoning Administrator can revoke a license after 3 or more ordinance violations in 6 months.
setback_notes: Enclosure must be at least 25 ft from any residential structure on an adjacent lot.
coop_rules: Chickens must be kept in a covered enclosure or a fenced enclosure at all times.
zoning_notes: Rule is citywide under Madison General Ordinances (MGO) Sec. 28.151; the city doubled its hen cap in past years (from 4 to 8) per Wisconsin Public Radio coverage.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

sources.name: City of Madison, Chicken License (official page)

research_notes: The city's own Chicken License page and search extracts of the Madison General Ordinances agree on the 8-hen cap, no-rooster rule, 25 ft setback, on-site slaughter ban and the state livestock-premises registration prerequisite; both searches returned matching detail from the same official source.
